chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Army bands in South Carolina and Alabama
summary: He served about four years, stuck in a weak South Carolina band that would not release him because he could read, before going to Oakland.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So after -- I don't know what Prez did after that. I went in the army before Prez, I believe, and then Prez followed me in the army. And I stayed in the army for four

years, and Prez stayed in for quite a while. He was in Alabama and I was -- of course I was all over. I didn't go out of the country, but in various bands. I was in the band in South Carolina, I think the best musician there could read about four bars. You know, that calibre of band. And I tried to get out and they -- they wouldn't let me out because I could play, you know. So they wanted someone, someone in here to play. And it was just brutal.
So I stayed with this band for a while, then I went to California, to Oakland, and that was nice.
